sentence: It's Thursday. Since Monday, Mina ___ three job applications.
setupText: Choose the form reporting a total completed between Monday and now.
taskText: It's Thursday. Since Monday, Mina ___ three job applications.
text: Choose the form reporting a total completed between Monday and now. It's Thursday. Since Monday, Mina ___ three job applications.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3881:Present perfect for a completed count
explanation: Has sent counts completed applications within a period that reaches the present Thursday.

rationales.is sending: 'Is sending' describes an activity in progress rather than the total already completed.
rationales.has sent: Has sent counts completed applications within a period that reaches the present Thursday.
rationales.sends: 'Sends' describes a routine, not an accumulated total since Monday.
rationales.had sent: Had sent counts back from a past reference point; this total is measured up to now.

sentence: I'll meet you outside when your bus ___ tomorrow.
setupText: Choose the standard form in this future time clause.
taskText: I'll meet you outside when your bus ___ tomorrow.
text: Choose the standard form in this future time clause. I'll meet you outside when your bus ___ tomorrow.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3882:Present simple in future time clauses
explanation: After 'when' in a future time clause, present simple can refer to tomorrow: 'when your bus arrives'.

rationales.arriving: 'Arriving' alone does not provide a complete verb after 'your bus'.
rationales.will arrive: 'Will arrive' works in a main prediction. In this standard future time clause after 'when', use the present form 'arrives'.
rationales.arrived: 'Arrived' puts the arrival in the past rather than in this open future arrangement.
rationales.arrives: After 'when' in a future time clause, present simple can refer to tomorrow: 'when your bus arrives'.

sentence: Aiko started practicing at nine. It's eleven and she is still at the piano: she ___ for two hours.
setupText: Choose the form emphasizing an activity that began earlier and is continuing now.
taskText: Aiko started practicing at nine. It's eleven and she is still at the piano: she ___ for two hours.
text: Choose the form emphasizing an activity that began earlier and is continuing now. Aiko started practicing at nine. It's eleven and she is still at the piano: she ___ for two hours.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3883:Present perfect continuous for ongoing duration
explanation: Has been practicing looks back over two hours of activity that continues at the present time.

rationales.has been practicing: Has been practicing looks back over two hours of activity that continues at the present time.
rationales.had practiced: Had practiced measures earlier practice from a past viewpoint, not from the present eleven o'clock.
rationales.will practice: 'Will practice' describes future practice, not the two hours already underway.
rationales.practices: Practices can state a routine of two-hour sessions; it does not express this continuing session from nine until now.

sentence: When I reached the station, Nadia ___; her train was already on its way.
setupText: Choose the form that explicitly places the departure before my arrival.
taskText: When I reached the station, Nadia ___; her train was already on its way.
text: Choose the form that explicitly places the departure before my arrival. When I reached the station, Nadia ___; her train was already on its way.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3884:Past perfect for earlier past completion
explanation: 'Had left' places Nadia's departure before another past event, my arrival at the station.

rationales.was leaving: Was leaving would put departure in progress at my arrival, not already over.
rationales.has left: Has left relates departure to now, but the reference point is my past arrival.
rationales.had left: 'Had left' places Nadia's departure before another past event, my arrival at the station.
rationales.is leaving: Is leaving gives a present viewpoint rather than the past sequence described.

sentence: My grandfather, who died in 2006, ___ as a chef for forty years.
setupText: Choose the ordinary tense for this finished biographical period.
taskText: My grandfather, who died in 2006, ___ as a chef for forty years.
text: Choose the ordinary tense for this finished biographical period. My grandfather, who died in 2006, ___ as a chef for forty years.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3885:Simple past for a finished duration
explanation: 'Worked' presents the forty-year career within a finished life period. 'For' can accompany simple past when the period is over.

rationales.has worked: Has worked connects a work history to a present period; this sentence explicitly closes his life and career in the past.
rationales.worked: 'Worked' presents the forty-year career within a finished life period. 'For' can accompany simple past when the period is over.
rationales.is working: Is working presents current work, which conflicts with the stated death.
rationales.will work: Will work places the career in the future, contrary to this completed biography.

sentence: If you've already paid online, you won't need to pay at the door.
setupText: Choose the interpretation of the present perfect in this condition.
taskText: If you've already paid online, you won't need to pay at the door.
text: Choose the interpretation of the present perfect in this condition. If you've already paid online, you won't need to pay at the door.
options: Earlier online payment removes the need to pay at the door.
Online payment will begin at the door.
Online payment is no longer possible.
answer: Earlier online payment removes the need to pay at the door.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3886:Present perfect in an open condition
explanation: "You've already paid" refers to payment completed before the relevant check. Present perfect is valid in an 'if' clause.

'Already paid' refers to completed payment, not payment beginning at the door.
The sentence says nothing about whether online payment remains available.
If leaves it open whether a particular person has paid; it does not claim everyone has.
rationales.Earlier online payment removes the need: "You've already paid" refers to payment completed before the relevant check. Present perfect is valid in an 'if' clause.

sentence: Before the supermarket was built, this corner ___ a small bakery.
setupText: Choose the form describing a past state that is no longer true.
taskText: Before the supermarket was built, this corner ___ a small bakery.
text: Choose the form describing a past state that is no longer true. Before the supermarket was built, this corner ___ a small bakery.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3887:Used to with a past state
explanation: 'Used to have' describes the former state of this corner and implies a change since then.

rationales.used to have: 'Used to have' describes the former state of this corner and implies a change since then.
rationales.would having: 'Would' cannot be followed by 'having'; for this former state, 'used to have' is the natural construction.
rationales.has had: Has had looks back from now rather than locating this state wholly before the supermarket was built.
rationales.is having: Is having presents a current activity and does not express this former state of possession.

sentence: Don't call at eight tomorrow evening. I ___ an online class then.

taskText: Don't call at eight tomorrow evening. I ___ an online class then.
text: Choose the form presenting an activity in progress at a future time. Don't call at eight tomorrow evening. I ___ an online class then.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3888:Future continuous at a specified moment
explanation: Will be attending places the class in progress at the future time when the call would interrupt it.

rationales.attended: 'Attended' describes past attendance, not tomorrow evening.
rationales.have attended: Have attended reports experience or completion before now.
rationales.will be attending: Will be attending places the class in progress at the future time when the call would interrupt it.
rationales.had attended: Had attended looks back from a past point rather than forward to tomorrow.

sentence: Rina ___ much happier since she ___ jobs last autumn.
setupText: Choose the pair that links a continuing situation to its past starting event.
taskText: Rina ___ much happier since she ___ jobs last autumn.
text: Choose the pair that links a continuing situation to its past starting event. Rina ___ much happier since she ___ jobs last autumn.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3889:Present perfect main clause with past since clause
explanation: Has been connects her happiness to now; changed names the finished past event that began that period.

rationales.was / has changed: 'Was' does not establish the continuing present situation, and 'has changed' does not fit the dated starting event 'last autumn'.
rationales.is being / changes: Is being suggests current behavior rather than a continuing state; changes does not locate the job change last autumn.
rationales.had been / changes: Had been needs a past reference point, while changes is present rather than the stated past starting event.
rationales.has been / changed: Has been connects her happiness to now; changed names the finished past event that began that period.

sentence: Mateo isn't here. He ___ to the pharmacy.

taskText: Mateo isn't here. He ___ to the pharmacy.
text: Choose the completion meaning Mateo is still away at the pharmacy. Mateo isn't here. He ___ to the pharmacy.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3890:Has gone versus has been
explanation: Has gone to the pharmacy presents his departure as resulting in his current absence.

rationales.has gone: Has gone to the pharmacy presents his departure as resulting in his current absence.
rationales.has been: Has been to normally reports a completed visit, often with a return, so it does not express the requested still-away meaning.
rationales.was going: Was going reports a past journey in progress or intention without establishing where he is now.
rationales.used to go: 'Used to go' describes a discontinued habit, not today's absence.

sentence: A decorator has paint on her hands. Some of the wall is still bare.
setupText: Choose the sentence that emphasizes a recent activity without saying the job is finished.
taskText: A decorator has paint on her hands. Some of the wall is still bare.
text: Choose the sentence that emphasizes a recent activity without saying the job is finished. A decorator has paint on her hands. Some of the wall is still bare.
options: The decorator has painted the whole wall.
The decorator painted the wall last year.
The decorator has been painting the wall.
The decorator will paint the wall tomorrow.
answer: The decorator has been painting the wall.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3891:Perfect continuous for recent activity and evidence
explanation: Has been painting focuses on recent activity with visible evidence now and does not claim the wall is finished.

rationales.The decorator has painted the whole wall: The whole wall makes a completion claim that conflicts with the bare section.
rationales.The decorator painted the wall last year: Last year's work does not describe the recent activity indicated by her hands.
rationales.The decorator has been painting the wall: Has been painting focuses on recent activity with visible evidence now and does not claim the wall is finished.
rationales.The decorator will paint the wall tomorr: 'Tomorrow' describes future work rather than the activity responsible for the current paint on her hands.

sentence: I ___ this flat is too small, so I ___ about moving.
setupText: Choose the pair that expresses a current opinion and a decision being considered now.
taskText: I ___ this flat is too small, so I ___ about moving.
text: Choose the pair that expresses a current opinion and a decision being considered now. I ___ this flat is too small, so I ___ about moving.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3892:State and activity senses of think
explanation: Think states an opinion; am thinking about describes the ongoing process of considering a move.

rationales.am thinking / think: This reverses the intended uses: the opinion takes think, while active consideration takes am thinking.
rationales.think / am thinking: Think states an opinion; am thinking about describes the ongoing process of considering a move.
rationales.thought / have thought: Thought places the opinion in the past, and have thought looks back on consideration rather than presenting it as underway now.
rationales.had thought / thought: Both forms locate thinking in the past, not in the two present meanings requested.

sentence: I ___ the curtains, but the shop closed before I got there.

taskText: I ___ the curtains, but the shop closed before I got there.
text: Choose the form expressing an intention that existed before the interruption. I ___ the curtains, but the shop closed before I got there.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3893:Was going to for a past intention
explanation: Was going to buy reports a past intention. The shop's closure explains why this planned purchase did not happen then.

rationales.have bought: Have bought says the purchase has happened, not that an earlier intention was interrupted.
rationales.am buying: Am buying presents a current arrangement or activity rather than the earlier plan.
rationales.buy: 'Buy' describes a present routine or narrative action, not the past intention requested.
rationales.was going to buy: Was going to buy reports a past intention. The shop's closure explains why this planned purchase did not happen then.

sentence: This is the quietest hotel I ___ at.

taskText: This is the quietest hotel I ___ at.
text: Choose the form comparing today's experience with all earlier experience up to now. This is the quietest hotel I ___ at.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3894:Present perfect in an experiential superlative
explanation: Have ever stayed compares this hotel with the speaker's experience up to the present.

rationales.have ever stayed: Have ever stayed compares this hotel with the speaker's experience up to the present.
rationales.will ever stay: Will ever stay extends the claim into the future, beyond the earlier experience requested.
rationales.had ever stayed: 'Had ever stayed' requires a past comparison point, as in 'That was the quietest hotel I had ever stayed at'.
rationales.am ever staying: Am ever staying does not form an experience comparison across previous visits.

sentence: The customer called at noon. The repair was already finished.

taskText: The customer called at noon. The repair was already finished.
text: Choose the sentence that says the repair was completed before the call. The customer called at noon. The repair was already finished.
options: Sara was repairing the bike when the customer called.
Sara repaired the bike after the customer called.
Sara would repair the bike after the customer called.
Sara had repaired the bike when the customer called.
answer: Sara had repaired the bike when the customer called.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3895:Reconstructing a past sequence from two statements
explanation: Had repaired presents the repair as complete by the past time of the call.

rationales.Sara was repairing the bike when the cus: Was repairing places the repair in progress at the call, not already complete.
rationales.Sara repaired the bike after the custome: After reverses the stated order: it puts the call first.
rationales.Sara had repaired the bike when the cust: Had repaired presents the repair as complete by the past time of the call.
rationales.Sara would repair the bike after the cus: Would repair looks forward from the call to a later repair, contrary to the stated order.

sentence: Don't switch off the computer until it has saved the file.
setupText: Choose the interpretation of the future instruction.
taskText: Don't switch off the computer until it has saved the file.
text: Choose the interpretation of the future instruction. Don't switch off the computer until it has saved the file.
options: Switch it off while saving is in progress.
Switch it off before saving starts.
Wait until someone starts editing the file.
Wait for saving to finish before switching it off.
answer: Wait for saving to finish before switching it off.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3896:Present perfect for completion in a future time clause
explanation: 'Until it has saved' makes completed saving the condition for switching off. Present perfect can refer to completion before a future action.

rationales.Switch it off while saving is in progres: Has saved presents saving as completed; switching off during saving would not meet the condition.
rationales.Wait for saving to finish before switchi: 'Until it has saved' makes completed saving the condition for switching off. Present perfect can refer to completion before a future action.
This reverses the instruction by switching off before the required saving.
rationales.Wait until someone starts editing the fi: Editing is a different action; the instruction's condition concerns saving.

sentence: On Monday, the guide promised that she ___ me the address the following day.
setupText: Choose the form reporting a future promise from a past viewpoint.
taskText: On Monday, the guide promised that she ___ me the address the following day.
text: Choose the form reporting a future promise from a past viewpoint. On Monday, the guide promised that she ___ me the address the following day.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3897:Would as future from a past reporting point
explanation: 'Would send' looks forward from the past promise to the following day; it is the reported counterpart of 'will send'.

rationales.has sent: Has sent reports a result before now, not a promise about a later day from Monday's viewpoint.
rationales.had sent: Had sent places sending before the promise, reversing the intended order.
rationales.sends: 'Sends' is present simple and does not express this future promise viewed from Monday.
rationales.would send: 'Would send' looks forward from the past promise to the following day; it is the reported counterpart of 'will send'.

sentence: '___ you ever visited Lisbon?' 'Yes, I ___ there in 2022.'

text: Choose the forms for a life-experience question followed by a dated answer. '___ you ever visited Lisbon?' 'Yes, I ___ there in 2022.'

explanation: Have you ever visited asks about experience up to now; went locates the visit in the finished year 2022.

rationales.Have / went: Have you ever visited asks about experience up to now; went locates the visit in the finished year 2022.
rationales.Did / have gone: The dated answer in 2022 needs went, not have gone, in this ordinary past account.

rationales.Do / am going: 'Do' cannot form 'do you ever visited', and 'am going' does not report a completed 2022 visit.

rationales.will live: Will live points forward from now, not to residence at that past time.

sentence: The forecast is uncertain. We will decide about the picnic tomorrow.
setupText: Choose the sentence treating tomorrow's rain as an open possibility.
taskText: The forecast is uncertain. We will decide about the picnic tomorrow.
text: Choose the sentence treating tomorrow's rain as an open possibility. The forecast is uncertain. We will decide about the picnic tomorrow.
options: If it had rained, we would have stayed inside.
If it rains, we'll stay inside.
If it rained yesterday, we stayed inside.
If it rains, we stayed inside yesterday.
answer: If it rains, we'll stay inside.
focusKey: coverage-verb-tense-b1-3900:Present form in an open future conditional
explanation: If it rains uses a present form for an open future condition; we'll stay gives the future result.

rationales.If it had rained, we would have stayed i: This imagines a different past outcome, not an open decision about tomorrow.
If it rains uses a present form for an open future condition; we'll stay gives the future result.
rationales.If it rained yesterday, we stayed inside: Yesterday and stayed place this condition and result in the past.
The stated result happened yesterday, so it cannot be the future picnic decision described.
